question: Which of the executable's imports are OS services, presentation, Steam or DRM (design 3.5), and how many static call sites does each have?
method: pefile reads the import directory; each dll!name is classified by a table keyed on DLL, with per-name groups for kernel32 and user32 (subclass) and a name override for user32!wvsprintfA. A linear iced-x86 decode of .text (padding skipped, one-byte resync on error) records every absolute memory operand equal to an IAT slot: call [slot] is a direct call site, jmp [slot] is a thunk, anything else a pointer load; every call rel32 or jmp rel32 targeting a thunk counts as a call to the thunk's import, and a 32-bit immediate equal to a thunk's address as a pointer load. Limits: static and linear, so data-in-code can hide or fabricate a reference and the counts are an upper bound on distinct sites, not a reachability proof; register-indirect calls through a loaded pointer are counted as pointer loads, not calls; PSFD00 is not swept; ordinal imports carry conventional names from public export tables that are not part of the input.

outputs.drm_note: no import names a CEG or DRM entry point; the unpacked executable is the lifter's input and CEG is never reached (design 3.5 d)
